title: VINEET SHARMA AND ORS versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010078572026
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc Application No. 982 of 2026
 Before the National Lok Adalat
Vineet Sharma and Ors --Applicants
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Another
--Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Ashish Sharma, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. Abhishek
Verma, learned counsel for the applicant.
Mr. Pradeep Lohani, learned AGA with Mr. Kuldeep Rawal, learned
AGA for the State.
Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for the respondent no.2 through
video conferencing.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
By means of this Application filed under
Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973,
the applicants have sought setting aside the cognizance
order dated 21.11.2025 as well as charge-sheet dated
02.07.2025 and entire proceedings of Criminal Case
No.1730 of 2025 (Case Crime No.0087 of 2023), "State
vs. Vineet Sharma & Others" pending before the court
of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Roorkee, District
Haridwar under Sections 498A, 323, 504 & 506 of IPC
and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Mr. Ashish Shrama, learned counsel for the
applicants-accused.
1

UKHC010078572026
3. Mr. Pradeep Lohani, learned AGA for the
State.
4. Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for the
respondent no.2.
5. Applicant no.1- Vineet Sharma who is the
husband of the respondent no.2 is present in-person.
Mr. Vinod Sharma and Smt. Sudesh Devi are present
through video conferencing, who are father-in-law and
mother-in-law of the respondent no.2 respectively.
They are duly identified by Mr. Ashish Sharma,
Advocate.
6. The respondent no.2 - Smt. Vartika Gautam
is present through video conferencing. She is duly
identified by Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate.
7. Both, the applicants and respondent no.2
submitted that they have filed a Compounding
Application (IA No.1 of 2026) and affidavits with their
free will and without any pressure. Today, they have
filed a Compromise Memo.
8. On interaction, respondent no.2 states that
she does not want to proceed with the said criminal
case. A divorce decree has already been passed. She
is requesting to quash the entire proceedings of the
2

UKHC010078572026
said Criminal Case No.1730 of 2025.
9. Both the parties submitted that they have
resolved their matrimonial disputes amicably. They
have filed a Compromise Memo.
10. Learned counsel for the State submitted that
there were matrimonial disputes between the parties
and they have resolved their disputes, therefore, the
State has no objection to the Compounding Application
(IA No.1 of 2026).
11. Keeping in view the totality of the facts and
circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that
ends of justice would be met if the compounding
application is allowed and the cognizance order dated
21.11.2025 as well as charge-sheet dated 02.07.2025
and entire proceedings of Criminal Case No.1730 of
2025 (Case Crime No.0087 of 2023), "State vs. Vineet
Sharma & Others" pending before the court of
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Roorkee, District
Haridwar under Sections 498A, 323, 504 & 506 of IPC
and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, are
quashed. Compounding application is accordingly
allowed.
12. Resultantly, the cognizance order dated
3

UKHC010078572026
21.11.2025 as well as charge-sheet dated 02.07.2025
and entire proceedings of Criminal Case No.1730 of
2025 (Case Crime No.0087 of 2023), "State vs. Vineet
Sharma & Others" pending before the court of
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Roorkee, District
Haridwar under Sections 498A, 323, 504 & 506 of IPC
and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, are
hereby quashed.
13. The Criminal Miscellaneous Application
(No.982 of 2026), filed under Section 482 of the Code
of Criminal Procedure, is disposed of accordingly.
14. The Compounding Application and the
Compromise Memo shall form part of this order.
